new_entities.name: Alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine (alpha-GPC)
new_entities.description: A choline-containing supplement marketed for cognitive and exercise-performance support.

new_entities.name: Anaerobic power output
new_entities.description: Peak or near-peak power production during short, high-intensity exercise tasks.

edges.population: healthy trained or recreationally active men
edges.mechanism: Alpha-GPC may transiently increase choline availability and cholinergic signaling, which could plausibly support neuromuscular drive during explosive efforts. In practice, the human data are inconsistent, with some signals for force or jump mechanics but little proof of a robust repeatable anaerobic-power benefit across protocols.
edges.summary: Evidence that alpha-GPC improves anaerobic power output is still preliminary and mixed. Small randomized trials show occasional gains in isolated force or jump-power outcomes, but null findings are common and one of the positive cycling studies used a multi-ingredient supplement that makes alpha-GPC-specific attribution impossible.
edges.caveats: The total evidence base is tiny, male-dominated, and built from short supplementation periods. Because several studies are underpowered or confounded by co-ingredients, this edge should be treated as speculative rather than established.
